title: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator detects open questions and answers them with web search
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned behaviour, rollout, licensing and documented controls, and explicitly flags Microsoft's conflicting statements about external meetings. One minor correction remains: the checklist asks administrators to check Facilitator app availability, but that control has no table row.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-11-13T19:41:44.
Microsoft plans for Facilitator to detect unanswered questions in Teams meetings and offer web-search answers.
claims.quote: Facilitator now automatically detects open questions raised during a Teams meeting and offers to help answer them using web search.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes an unanswered question such as 'What is an LLM?' followed by an offer that participants can accept with Yes.
claims.quote: When a participant asks a question (e.g., “What is an LLM?”) and no one answers, Facilitator posts a prompt offering to find an answer. Participants can select “Yes” to have the agent retrieve and share the information.

claims.claim: Allow web search in Copilot is a general Copilot policy available in Cloud Policy, with its precise application to Facilitator left unconfirmed.
claims.quote: The primary way that IT admins can control access to web search is by using the Allow web search in Copilot policy, which is available only in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: For the commercial cloud in scope, web search is available when its policy is unconfigured unless optional connected experiences are disabled.
claims.quote: If the IT admin doesn't configure the Allow web search in Copilot policy, web search will be available to users in both Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat, unless the IT admin has set the Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office policy to Disabled.

claims.where: Open questions: Allow web search in Copilot
claims.claim: The general web-search policy includes an option to disable search in Copilot Work mode.
claims.quote: Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat

claims.claim: Cloud Policy creation follows Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. ... On the Policy configurations page, select Create. ... On the Start with the basics page ... On the Choose the scope page ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration.

claims.claim: No API for the Cloud Policy web-search policy is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Cloud Policy Allow web search Copilot Microsoft Graph API PowerShell policy configuration automation; "Cloud Policy" "Microsoft Graph" API configurations. Read Cloud Policy overview and web-search controls; results document UI and audit APIs, not policy-setting automation.

claims.claim: No separate UI or API switch for proactive question detection and answers is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Facilitator" "proactive" "settings"; "Facilitator" "questions" "Set-CsTeams". Read facilitator-teams and MC1409304: app availability, web search and the notes-only PowerShell setting are described; no separate proactive-Q&A switch is documented.

claims.claim: Facilitator AI interactions in meetings are retained using a retention policy with the Teams chats location.
claims.quote: For Facilitator AI interactions in meetings, use a retention policy with the Teams chats option.

claims.claim: The retention-policy path is Microsoft Purview portal > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention Policies.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, navigate to Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention Policies

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -TeamsChatLocation <locations> creates the Teams-chat retention policy, with a rule additionally required as the prose explains.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... The Name parameter specifies the unique name of the retention policy. ... The TeamsChatLocation parameter specifies the Teams users to include in the policy.

claims.claim: A retention policy also requires a rule created using New-RetentionComplianceRule.
claims.quote: Creating a new policy also requires use of the New-RetentionComplianceRule cmdlet. ... Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies)

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn documents Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Facilitator from the app list. ... In the actions menu, select Allow or Block. ... In the pop-up, select the Allow or Block button.

claims.claim: Learn says the Facilitator app is allowed by default.
claims.quote: Facilitator is allowed by default.

claims.claim: The documented Allow or Block procedure calls for Teams admin credentials.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center with your Teams admin credentials.

claims.claim: Facilitator is blocked if all apps are blocked for the organisation.
claims.quote: However, if all apps are blocked for your organization, Facilitator is also blocked.

claims.claim: The Facilitator page describes app permission policies and app-centric management for allowing groups of users.
claims.quote: Follow the instructions at Use app permission policies to control user access to apps to create a new app policy for Facilitator. ... Follow the instructions at Add or modify app availability for users to assign the policy to users using app-centric management.

claims.claim: After migration, app availability is edited on the app's Users and groups tab through Availability > Edit availability.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. ... Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. ... Select Edit availability.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents Update-M365TeamsApp for managing app availability under app-centric management.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsAppPermissionPolicy warning requires creation and modification of app permission policies in the admin centre, rather than prohibiting app-centric PowerShell.
claims.quote: We require that all creation and modification of app permission polices (not including the assignment or removal of policies from users) happens in the Microsoft Teams & Skype for Business Admin Center

claims.claim: Blocking Facilitator governs the app as a whole, not only proactive answers, and therefore removes access to its notes and other skills.
claims.quote: As an admin, you control whether Facilitator is available to your entire organization or to a certain group of users. ... To allow or block Facilitator for users, complete the following steps:

claims.claim: Purview auditing supports Facilitator, including questions and answers for meetings.
claims.quote: Auditing and AI interactions ... Facilitator AI-generated notes, moderation, and questions and answers for meetings are supported.

claims.claim: Purview eDiscovery supports Facilitator questions and answers for meetings.
claims.quote: eDiscovery and AI interactions ... Facilitator AI-generated notes, moderation, and questions and answers for meetings are supported with a KeyQL query.

claims.claim: Purview Data Lifecycle Management supports Facilitator AI interactions in meetings.
claims.quote: | Data Lifecycle Management | **✓** | ... For Facilitator AI interactions in meetings, use a retention policy with the Teams chats option.
